title: Routing Orchestrator: Visual Policy Lab and Preview Flow
creator: Lena Chen
description: Deliver a customer-facing visual 'Policy Lab' inside Redwood Console where users author, validate, and preview routing rules that combine region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. The Lab will: 1) expose a drag-and-drop rule builder for region + tier constraints and variant fallbacks, 2) run deterministic validation with explainable error messages, 3) generate a simulated request trace preview (latency/cost/SLA impact) and a synthetic traffic rehearsal mode, and 4) surface suggested fixes and telemetry for production rollout guidance.
background: Customers repeatedly ask for a single place to encode complex fallback strategies (region-first, tier-priority, model-variant fallback) and to understand the cost/latency tradeoffs before hitting production. Current console screens are fragmented: region selector, tier dropdowns, and a separate rollout preview. That fragmentation causes misconfigurations and unexpected failovers. This initiative consolidates that UX and plugs in validation and a lightweight simulator.
proposal:
- UI: 'Policy Lab' canvas with left-hand palette (conditions: geo region, latency SLA, cost budget, customer tier) and right-hand rule inspector.
- Authoring: users can chain clauses (e.g., if region IN (eu-west, eu-central) AND customer_tier >= enterprise THEN route to model X-quantized ELSE route to model Y) and attach a fallback list with ordered model variants.
- Validation: static checks (incompatible model and region, quota mismatches, unsupported quantization on Dedicated pools) plus runtime heuristics (estimated cold-start risk). Validation messages include remediation suggestions.
- Preview: simulate N synthetic requests per second with adjustable distribution (percent by geo, sequence length). Output shows per-route expected p99 latency, token cost delta, and likely fallback events.
- Telemetry: export preview to a shareable URL and write a pre-rollout checklist (safety checks, cost delta, canary policy recommended).
engineering_notes: Frontend: build canvas with reusable rule components and JSON import/export
Backend: reuse routing engine validator endpoint (ENG-12892) and add a preview simulator sandbox that runs off a cost/latency profile service
Need new API: POST /preview/policy-simulate that accepts policy JSON and distribution config
Performance: simulator must run within 10s for 1000-sample preview for good UX
acceptance_criteria: Users can create a multi-clause policy combining region + tier + fallback variants in the console
Static validation surfaces at least 10 common misconfigurations with clear remediation text
Preview returns per-route latency and cost estimates for a user-provided traffic distribution within 15s
Exportable preview link created and can be consumed by invited teammates
End-to-end tests and e2e CI added; feature gated behind rollout flag for 10% of orgs
qa_plan: Unit tests for rule parser and validator
Integration test for preview API with mocked cost/latency profiles
Manual UX pass with 3 internal customers (SE, PM, Solutions) and 2 pilot customers
Run chaos scenario where primary region is force-failed and confirm fallback ordering honored
